examples.text: Dies wird seine Neugierde erwecken.
Die Ausstellung hat bei jungen Leuten großes Interesse erweckt.
examples.translation: The exhibition has aroused a lot of interest among young people.
examples.english: The exhibition has aroused a lot of interest among young people.

glosses: перен. возбуждать, вызывать (интерес и т. п.)

examples.text: Oran erweckte damals, zum Beispiel um drei Uhr nachmittags und bei schönem Wetter, den trügerischen Eindruck einer ein Fest feiernden Stadt, deren Verkehr man gesperrt und Geschäfte man geschlossen hat, damit eine öffentliche Veranstaltung stattfinden kann, und deren Einwohner auf die Straßen geströmt sind, um an den Festlichkeiten teilzunehmen.
examples.translation: Oran donnait alors, vers trois heures de l’après-midi par exemple, et sous un beau ciel, l’impression trompeuse d’une cité en fête dont on eût arrêté la circulation et fermé les magasins pour permettre le déroulement d’une manifestation publique, et dont les habitants eussent envahi les rues pour participer aux réjouissances.

glosses: jemanden wach machen, zum Leben bringen

examples.text: Dein Geschrei kann ja Tote erwecken.
„In Wüsten erweckt erst der Regen einige Pflanzen zum Leben. Andere überleben die Dürre, indem sie Wasser in ihren Stängeln oder Wurzeln speichern.“
Er hat damit nur falsche Hoffnungen erweckt.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: jemanden wach machen, zum Leben bringen

examples.text: to arouse compassion, jealousy, or anger

“My tastes,” he said, still smiling, “incline me to the garishly sunlit side of this planet.” And, to tease her and arouse her to combat: “I prefer a farandole to a nocturne ; I'd rather have a painting than an etching ; Mr. Whistler bores me with his monochromatic mud; I don't like dull colours, dull sounds, dull intellects;[…].”
She removed Stranleigh’s coat with a dexterity that aroused his imagination.

His unruly hair was slicked down with water, and as Jessamy introduced him to Miss Brindle his face assumed a cherubic innocence which would immediately have aroused the suspicions of anyone who knew him.

[…] grinding against their partners like burlesque performers, which even in parody Terry found erotic—reminding him of the Persian belly dancer he'd seen at the college, whose sensual dancing aroused him despite her claim of high art.

glosses: To cause an erection of the penis or other physical signs of sexual arousal, such as fluid secretion.

examples.text: I can't wear wool underwear: it tends to arouse me at inappropriate times.

glosses: To wake from sleep or stupor; to rouse.

examples.text: He kenned not whether it was devil or mortal, but flung himself on the roadside and lay like a corp for an hour or more, till the rain aroused him.

1996, Beruga (line translated by Dan Owsen), Terranigma. Nintendo of America.
I have no idea who you are, but I thank you for arousing me.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: jemanden wach machen, zum Leben bringen

examples.text: Be careful how you touch her, she'll awaken / As sleep's the only freedom all that she knows / And when you walk into her eyes, you won't believe / The way she's always paying for a debt she never owes
Each morning he awakens with a smile on his face.

glosses: To bring into action (something previously dormant); to stimulate.

examples.text: Awaken your entrepreneurial spirit!
We hope to awaken your interest in our programme.
On the other hand, the self-cleaning smokebox belongs to the latter-day period of the L.M.S.R., when the visiting U.S.A. 2-8-0s of the war had awakened an interest in such things.
I'll miss the sea. But a person needs new experiences. They draw something deep inside, allowing him to grow. Without change, something sleeps inside us and seldom awakens. The sleeper must awaken.

glosses: To call to a sense of sin.

examples.text: [This ant] I ſuffered to lye above an hour in the Spirit; and after I had taken it out, and put its body and legs into a natural poſture, remained moveleſs about an hour; but then , upon a ſudden, as if it had been awaken out of a drunken ſleep, it ſuddenly reviv'd and ran away...

I was completely taken in, and departed without making the assessment. However, when whole flatsful began to make similar explanations under similar circumstances, I awoke to the fact that I had been bluffed.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: jemanden wach machen, zum Leben bringen

examples.text: I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. […] The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.

glosses: To become more aware of a real-life situation; to concentrate on the matter in hand.

examples.text: Some businesses were slow to wake up to the importance of the Internet.
That's the third time you've made the same mistake. Wake up!

glosses: Interrumpir el sueño de quien duerme.

Hacer nacer o revivir en la mente o en el espíritu alguna idea, recuerdo, emoción, sentimiento, sensación, etc. que estaba olvidado o latente. (Despertar el apetito. Despertar un recuerdo. Despertar el deseo de viajar)
Hacer que una persona perciba que estaba engañada o equivocada.
Dejar de dormir, quitarse el sueño.\n:*Uso: se emplea también como pronominal
Avivarse el espíritu, volverse menos ingenuo, más penetrante.

To cause the manifestation of something (emotion, picture, etc.) in someone's mind or imagination.

examples.text: The book evokes a detailed and lively picture of what life was like in the 19th century.
